call_points.text: FY27 disbursement growth guided at 22-23% and AUM growth at 17-18%.
Branch network expanded to 440 across 15 states.
Home loan disbursements grew 38% YoY; management aims to regain home loan market share.
Cost of funds improved 38 bps YoY; PLR cut 10 bps in June, cumulative 25 bps since March 2026.
Net worth ₹5,220 Cr; CAR 44.66%, well above regulatory requirements.
RBI circular on asset classification of repossessed assets is under evaluation; no quantified impact yet.
Productivity per field resource targeted to double from ₹8-10 lakh to ₹20-22 lakh over two years.
Added 31 branches in Q4, taking the network to 435 branches across 15 states.
Q4 disbursements of ₹23.5 billion grew 16% YoY and 36% QoQ.
Secured ~₹975 Cr (USD 108 million) NCD commitment, the largest in company history.
Net worth ₹50.5 billion with CRAR at 44.6%, well above regulatory requirement.
Loan volumes were flat in FY26 and home-loan volumes fell YoY despite branch and staff expansion.
Management is watching Middle East war and inflation but has seen no bounce or collection deterioration so far.
Balance transfer out closed FY26 at 5.5%, within the under-6% guidance.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Alleged penalty on disallowance under Section 36(1)(va) of Income-tax Act 1961. Penalty is unwarranted in case of difference of opinion, it is in process of taking matter to upper appellate forum
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Income-tax Assessment Unit / Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals)
tax_litigation.status: The Hon’ble Tribunal of Jaipur has quashed the order of Commissioner Appeal and deleted the penalty of Rs.2,07,484 vide order dated 22 September 2026. The order giving effect to the said order by the jurisdictional officer is yet to be passed.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Order u/s 73 of the DGST Act, 2017 with regard to Input Tax Credit for value Rs. 2,67,105 (includes tax, interest & penalty). Company is in process of filing appeal against the aforesaid matter
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, Delhi

guidance.statement: Aspiration to consistently deliver 20%-plus AUM growth, largely to outperform industry
Credit costs to remain below 25 bps on a sustainable basis
Opex to AUM to fall below 3% over 2-3 years and to 2.75% at double the balance sheet
FY27 disbursement growth of 22-23% and AUM growth of 17-18%
Spread expected to fall below 5% for FY27

industry: Financial Services > Finance > Housing Finance Company

operating_notes.text: 1+ DPD was 3.17% and GNPA 1.05% at Mar-2026, with total ECL provisioning of ₹1.3 billion.
Borrowing mix: 40% linked to external benchmarks (repo, T-Bill, MIBOR) and 33% to up to 3-month MCLR, repricing 73% of borrowing quickly.
Liquidity at Mar-2026 included cash and unavailed cash credit limits of ₹19 billion and documented unavailed sanctions of ₹9.75 billion.
Q1FY27 disbursements were ₹1,610 Cr, up 41% YoY, with June disbursements above ₹600 Cr.
Branch network stood at 440 across 15 states as of June 2026.
42% of borrowings are linked to external benchmarks and 34% to sub-3-month MCLR, enabling re-pricing of 76% of borrowings.

timeline.summary: On 5 May 2026 Aavas held its Q4FY26 earnings call, where new CEO Manu Singh set a 20%-plus AUM growth aspiration and management reported Q4 PAT up 18% to ₹182 Cr with GNPA at 1.05%.

On July 21, 2026, Aavas Financiers held its Q1FY27 earnings call, reporting 23% YoY PAT growth to ₹171 Cr, 15.4% AUM growth to ₹23,930 Cr, and guiding FY27 AUM growth of 17-18% with spread expected below 5%.
